title: الْمَصْدَر (al-maṣdar : the Verbal Noun) — the Act Itself, Detached from Person and Time
summary: A deliberately shortened session, since some of the students were fasting, which finishes the أَمَّا answers of tamrīn 14 and then slows down to explain الْمَصْدَر properly. The teacher shows that every verb has a noun form naming the bare act — ذَهَبَ، يَذْهَبُ، الذَّهَاب — which is tied to no person and no tense, behaves like any اسْم in taking أل or tanwīn, and appears all over the Qur'ān and everyday signage.
key_points: Arabic words fall into three categories: اسْم (ism : noun), فِعْل (fiʿl : verb), and حَرْف (ḥarf : particle). الْمَصْدَر belongs to the first even though it carries the meaning of the second.

الْمَصْدَر (al-maṣdar) is the noun form of a verb, naming the act itself: ذَهَبَ (he went), يَذْهَبُ (he is going), and الذَّهَاب (adh-dhahāb : the act of going) — the last attached to no particular person and no particular time.
Because it is a noun, a مَصْدَر can carry أل or tanwīn — دُخُول or الدُّخُول — whereas a verb never takes أل.
Familiar words are مَصَادِر already: السُّجُود (as-sujūd : prostrating) from سَجَدَ، يَسْجُدُ، and الرُّكُوع (ar-rukūʿ) from رَكَعَ، يَرْكَعُ.
Many مَصَادِر of this lesson share one pattern, فُعُول: دُخُول (entering), خُرُوج (leaving), نُزُول (descending), جُلُوس (sitting), رُكُوب (riding).
There is no shortcut for predicting a مَصْدَر's exact form — the teacher's answer was that you learn each with time.
Some scholars hold the مَصْدَر to be the original word from which the verbs are themselves extracted, though there is اِخْتِلَاف (ikhtilāf : difference of opinion) on this.
اللِّقَاء (al-liqāʾ : the meeting) is the مَصْدَر of لَقِيَ، يَلْقَى, which is why أَنَا مَسْرُورٌ بِلِقَائِكَ literally means I am delighted at the meeting of you.
الْأَمَان (al-amān : safety) is the مَصْدَر of أَمِنَ، يَأْمَنُ, giving فِي أَمَانِ اللَّهِ — in the protection of Allah عَزَّ وَجَلَّ. The name أَمِينَة is not a مَصْدَر but an اسْم الفَاعِل.
To ask a price, attach the بَاء of price to كَمْ: بِكَمْ هَذَا (bi-kam hādhā : for how much is this), answered with هَذَا بِعَشَرَةِ رِيَالَاتٍ.
سَنَة (sanah : year) pluralises as سَنَوَات or سِنِين, the latter being the form usually found in the Qur'ān; قَرِيب (qarīb : a relative) pluralises as أَقَارِب.
عُثْمَان is غَيْر مُنْصَرِف (ghayr munṣarif : a diptote), so it takes a ḍamma without tanwīn as the فَاعِل: يَدْرُسُ حَامِدٌ وَعُثْمَانُ.
questions: [00:05:05] Q: Where does نَسِيَ occur in the Qur'ān? — A: In several places, including Mūsā عَلَيْهِ السَّلَام and the boy forgetting the fish, Ādam عَلَيْهِ السَّلَام forgetting the command, and the one who turns from Allah's remembrance being told كَذَٰلِكَ أَتَتْكَ آيَاتُنَا فَنَسِيتَهَا.
[00:19:00] Q: Does the مَصْدَر follow a specific format? — A: It is a noun, so it follows noun rules — it can take أل or tanwīn — rather than verb rules.
[00:21:00] Q: How do you know the exact form of a given مَصْدَر? — A: There is no rule to lean on; you learn each one with exposure over time.
[00:23:02] Q: Does the ḥadīth about loving the meeting of Allah refer to the Day of Judgement? — A: It refers to the hereafter in general rather than that day specifically.

[00:24:01] Q: Wouldn't everyone be afraid to meet Allah عَزَّ وَجَلَّ? — A: Dread arising from one's own shortcomings does not negate love; the ḥadīth concerns love for Allah, much as one may love one's parents while dreading facing them after a mistake.
[00:25:00] Q: Why are girls named أَمِينَة if أَمِنَ means he was safe? — A: أَمِينَة is an اسْم الفَاعِل, the one who is safe or trustworthy, not the مَصْدَر أَمَان.
[00:27:00] Q: What word is used for exit on signs? — A: الْخُرُوج, the مَصْدَر of خَرَجَ، يَخْرُجُ, or sometimes مَخْرَج.

quiz.a: The teacher's defining point: الذَّهَاب is the bare act of going, attached to no particular person and no tense.

quiz.q: Which of the three categories of Arabic words does a مَصْدَر belong to?
options: It forms a fourth category of its own
quiz.a: It is an اسْم that happens to carry verbal meaning, which is why it follows noun rules.

quiz.q: Which test shows that a مَصْدَر is a noun and not a verb?
options: It can carry أل or tanwīn, which a verb never can
It can be negated with لَا
It changes with the gender of the speaker
quiz.a: The teacher noted that verbs never take أل, while دُخُول or الدُّخُول are both acceptable.

quiz.q: What is the مَصْدَر of دَخَلَ، يَدْخُلُ?
quiz.a: دُخُول is the act of entering — the form seen on doors reading هَذَا الْبَابُ لِلدُّخُولِ.

quiz.a: The teacher pointed out that this run of مَصَادِر stays on one pattern, so students could continue the exercise by analogy.

quiz.q: What is اللِّقَاء the مَصْدَر of?
quiz.a: لَقِيَ means he met and يَلْقَى he is meeting, so اللِّقَاء is the meeting itself — hence مَسْرُورٌ بِلِقَائِكَ.

quiz.q: Why is أَمِينَة not a مَصْدَر?
options: Because it is an اسْم الفَاعِل, the one who is safe
Because it is a proper name only
quiz.a: The مَصْدَر of أَمِنَ is أَمَان; أَمِينَة names the one possessing that quality, which is an اسْم الفَاعِل.

quiz.q: How do you ask the price of something?
quiz.a: The بَاء of price is attached to كَمْ, so بِكَمْ هَذَا, answered with هَذَا بِعَشَرَةِ رِيَالَاتٍ.

quiz.q: Which plural of سَنَة is the one normally used in the Qur'ān?
quiz.a: Both سَنَوَات and سِنِين are plurals of سَنَة, and the teacher noted that سِنِين is the form generally found in the Qur'ān.

quiz.q: Why does عُثْمَان appear as عُثْمَانُ without tanwīn when it is the فَاعِل?
options: Because it is غَيْر مُنْصَرِف, a diptote
Because proper nouns never take tanwīn
quiz.a: The teacher identified عُثْمَان as غَيْر مُنْصَرِف, so it takes the ḍamma of the فَاعِل but no tanwīn.

quran_examples.arabic: فَإِنِّي نَسِيتُ الْحُوتَ وَمَا أَنسَانِيهُ إِلَّا الشَّيْطَانُ أَنْ أَذْكُرَهُ
quran_examples.transliteration: fa-innī nasītu al-ḥūta wa-mā ansānīhu illā al-shayṭānu an adhkurah
quran_examples.translation: Indeed, I forgot the fish, and none made me forget it except Satan, that I should mention it.
quran_examples.note: The first āyah offered when the class traced نَسِيَ (to forget) through the Qur'ān, during the vocabulary of tamrīn 14.

quran_examples.arabic: وَلَقَدْ عَهِدْنَا إِلَىٰ آدَمَ مِن قَبْلُ فَنَسِيَ وَلَمْ نَجِدْ لَهُ عَزْمًا
quran_examples.transliteration: wa-laqad ʿahidnā ilā ādama min qablu fa-nasiya wa-lam najid lahu ʿazmā
quran_examples.translation: And We had already taken a promise from Ādam before, but he forgot, and We found in him no firm resolve.
quran_examples.note: Cited for نَسِيَ, with the teacher noting it shows forgetting rather than deliberate intent.

quran_examples.arabic: قَالَ رَبِّ لِمَ حَشَرْتَنِي أَعْمَىٰ وَقَدْ كُنتُ بَصِيرًا ۝ قَالَ كَذَٰلِكَ أَتَتْكَ آيَاتُنَا فَنَسِيتَهَا وَكَذَٰلِكَ الْيَوْمَ تُنسَىٰ
quran_examples.transliteration: qāla rabbi lima ḥashartanī aʿmā wa-qad kuntu baṣīrā, qāla kadhālika atatka āyātunā fa-nasītahā wa-kadhālika al-yawma tunsā
quran_examples.translation: He will say: My Lord, why have you raised me blind when I used to see? He will say: Thus did Our signs come to you, and you forgot them; so today you will be forgotten.
quran_examples.note: The teacher walked through these āyāt word by word while explaining نَسِيَ, also glossing لِمَ as why and أَعْمَى as blind.
A student's answer for where صَعِدَ، يَصْعَدُ (to rise) occurs in the Qur'ān, the verb behind مِصْعَد (elevator).

quran_examples.arabic: فَمَن يُرِدِ اللَّهُ أَن يَهْدِيَهُ يَشْرَحْ صَدْرَهُ لِلْإِسْلَامِ ۚ وَمَن يُرِدْ أَن يُضِلَّهُ يَجْعَلْ صَدْرَهُ ضَيِّقًا حَرَجًا كَأَنَّمَا يَصَّعَّدُ فِي السَّمَاءِ
quran_examples.transliteration: fa-man yuridi llāhu an yahdiyahu yashraḥ ṣadrahu li-l-islām, wa-man yurid an yuḍillahu yajʿal ṣadrahu ḍayyiqan ḥarajan ka-annamā yaṣṣaʿʿadu fī al-samāʾ
quran_examples.translation: So whoever Allah wants to guide, He expands his breast for Islam; and whoever He wants to misguide, He makes his breast tight and constricted, as though he were climbing into the sky.
quran_examples.note: Raised as a second, intensified form of the same root صَعِدَ, and explained in full when a student asked about it.
